title: Milt Jackson's perfect pitch and photographic memory
summary: Heath describes Milt recalling complicated fugues after a year's gap when John played a passage.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Now Milt also had perfect pitch and a photographic memory, right?

Yes sir. We discontinued playing some of those really complicated fugues for a year or so, and John would say, “Milt, why don’t we play so-and-so again?” and Jackson would start into it and he’d stumble into one spot, and he’d say, “What did I do here?” And John would play it on the piano, and he’d say, “Oh yeah!” and he’d get the whole composition like we played it yesterday. That’s what Jackson could do.
